raw_response:
# C14 — Baseline B

I found three potentially useful components or mechanisms through opened awesome-list catalogues. These are internal-model translations to the stated problem, not claims of deployment or a complete language design. Every accepted candidate was listed in the opened [Awesome Python catalogue](https://github.com/batermj/awesome-python-1) before its primary source was opened.

1. **[Effect — intent objects with separate performers](https://github.com/python-effect/effect).** Effect's separation of an inert intent from its performer could help keep annotation descriptions available while deferring name lookup and arbitrary evaluation until a consumer requests them. The transfer would require explicit rules for namespaces, caching, errors, and existing consumers. It is an analogy rather than an annotation implementation. **Date status: unknown.** The live README references 2015 talks, but the attempted talk and package-history links failed; I did not verify a dated version of the API.

2. **[SymPy — symbolic expression representation](https://github.com/sympy/sympy).** SymPy's Symbol-based expression objects suggest storing an annotation's unresolved names as expression data instead of requiring their Python values during function definition. This supports a representation idea, but SymPy's mathematical semantics and import cost make it unsuitable as a direct general-annotation dependency. A language implementation would still need to preserve arbitrary Python expressions and non-type metadata. **Date status: unknown.** The opened README demonstrates symbolic expression construction and cites a January 2017 paper; the paper's DOI returned HTTP 403.

3. **[mypy — optional static checking separate from execution](https://github.com/python/mypy).** Mypy's separate static-checking phase provides a consumer model in which type hints can remain optional and be checked without executing the annotated program. It does not itself remove definition-time evaluation or provide an arbitrary-metadata evaluator. **Date status: pre-decision for this separation mechanism.** The [original news archive](https://www.mypy-lang.org/news.html) explicitly dates the checking/execution separation to 2014-08-31 and records variable-annotation support on 2016-10-07; this does not backdate every feature on the current README.

The main transferable combination is an unevaluated representation, an explicit interpretation step, and an optional static consumer. That is my inference from these components. None of the opened evidence establishes a finished solution covering forward references, import cost, dynamic typing, and arbitrary annotation uses together.

The run used four exact search queries and 24 conservatively counted retrieval attempts, including failed requests, repeated reads, and find-on-page operations. Search snippets returned outside the catalogue restrictions were not accepted as discovery evidence. Forbidden proposal snippets and adjacent annotation-design material encountered in those results are recorded in exposures. The model may have pretraining knowledge; memory leakage is not controlled.
